options: Practising trades with pretend money at real prices, recording them as if real
questions.why: It lets you test ideas, rules and your own behaviour without risking real money.

questions.q: Match each market to its usual hours (UK time).
pairs: Sunday night to Friday night, almost round the clock
questions.why: Hours matter: pick a market you can actually watch when you need to.

questions.q: Paper trading feels just the same as trading real money, so results transfer exactly.
questions.why: Pretend losses don't hurt like real ones, so people often trade more boldly on paper. Size paper trades realistically.

questions.q: Why should you write the reason for a trade in your journal before entering it?
options: Afterwards it's too easy to invent a convincing story
It makes the trade more likely to win
questions.why: Hindsight makes every trade look sensible. A written plan beforehand keeps you honest.

questions.q: You risked {r} on a paper trade (the gap to your stop × size) and made {p}. What's the result in R?
Put the steps for a first paper trade in order.
items: Choose a market and watch it for a week
Write a simple entry and exit rule
Fill in setup, entry, stop, target and size in the journal
Enter the trade and leave the stop alone
Record the result and whether you followed your rules
questions.why: Learn the market, set rules, plan in writing, execute, then review honestly.

questions.q: What does the FCA say about crypto for ordinary investors?
options: It's high risk and mostly unregulated: be prepared to lose all the money you put in
Crypto CFDs are fine for beginners
It's as safe as a savings account
questions.why: Most crypto isn't regulated, there's usually no FSCS cover, and crypto derivatives are banned for retail customers.

questions.q: A provider's demo account is always set up to help you trade carefully.
questions.why: Many demos encourage high leverage and frequent trading, because that's how providers earn. Set your own realistic rules.

questions.q: Why is it usually better for a beginner to focus on one market?
options: You learn how it behaves: its hours, spreads, typical moves and news
Other markets are illegal for beginners
One market always beats the others
It's the only way to avoid tax
questions.why: Depth beats breadth: knowing one market well makes your journal and results meaningful.

questions.q: Explain two things to consider when choosing which market to paper trade.

ideas.label: Its trading hours versus when you can watch it
How volatile it is versus your nerves and risk

questions.model: Its trading hours (can you watch it when it matters?), how volatile it is compared with your nerves and risk limits, and its costs and regulation (spreads, fees, and whether it's FCA-regulated, unlike most crypto).
questions.why: The right market fits your life, your nerves and your costs.

tests.answer: Whether its hours fit my school day, how volatile it is for my nerves, and the spreads and regulation.

questions.q: Explain why a trading journal helps you tell skill from luck.

ideas.label: It records every trade, wins and losses, so you see the real overall results
Over many trades you can check whether results come from following rules or chance (patterns, expectancy)

questions.model: A journal records every trade, including losses we'd rather forget, so you see your real results. Over many trades you can check whether profits come from following your rules (an edge) or just a lucky streak, and spot patterns in your mistakes.

tests.answer: It records all trades including losses, and over many trades shows whether following my rules works or it was luck.
It keeps a record of your trades.
It makes trades win more often.
